chapters.title: Chapter 11: Landmark Case—In re E.I. du Pont de Nemours & Co.
chapters.reason: DuPont is the foundational precedent that enumerates and frames the thirteen-factor likelihood-of-confusion test and its flexible balancing approach. Verbatim excerpts of the opinion (factor list, rationale, and guidance on weighing) are essential to accurately teach the doctrine and to cite the controlling language students and practitioners will rely on.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Landmark Cases—Crowded Fields and Relatedness of Goods/Services
chapters.reason: This chapter synthesizes multiple leading opinions (Juice Generation, Jack Wolfskin, Palm Bay, Coach Services, Olde Tyme Foods) that develop the 'crowded field' doctrine, standards for third‑party use/registration evidence, and the relatedness inquiry. Excerpts of the key holdings and factual reasoning are needed to show how courts articulate evidentiary thresholds and apply those precedents across DuPont factors 1, 2, and 6.
